label: Aristotle, Physics VII.1, 242b23-27: If each member of an infinite chain touches or is continuous…
interpretation: Typed reading over chains indexed by the natural numbers: if each member touches or is continuous with the next, some one thing is made of them all (242b26: ὥστʼ εἶναί τι ἐξ ἁπάντων ἕν). The -A reading states the same step for the hypothesised chain with atoms. The reading does not say whether the one thing is finite or infinite; 242b27-29 says this makes no difference. Chains are injective (infinitely many distinct members: ἄπειρα τὰ κινοῦντα, 242b12; ἀπείρων ὄντων, 242b29), so a finite cycle of mutual movers is not such a chain and is not excluded. The sentence is said of the hypothesised chain; the reading generalizes it to every injective touching chain.
